question: How much time was taken to frame the Constitution of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2 years, 11 months and 18 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The total time taken to frame the constitution was 2 years 11 months and 18 days.**
 
• Rajendra Prasad was appointed as the permanent President during its meeting on 11th December 1946.
 
• Dr B. R. Ambedkar studied the constitutions of about 60 countries while drafting the constitution.
 
 
• He was chairman of the drafting committee and is recognized as the **"Father of the Indian Constitution".**
 
 
 
• After the partition of India, the number of members of the** Constituent Assembly came to 299, of whom 284 were actually present on 26 November 1949 **and signed the final approved Constitution of the Indian Assembly, which had been elected for undivided India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The constitutional assembly of India got the status of a sovereign body through the Indian independent act of 1947.
 
• An idea for a Constituent Assembly was proposed in 1934 by M. N. Roy, a pioneer of the Communist movement in India.
 
• The Constituent Assembly met for the first time on 9 December 1946, reassembling on **14 August 1947 **as a sovereign body and successor to the British parliament's authority in India.
